title: Anchorless golden probe with contextual perturbation and randomized fidelity checks
creator: Riley Chen
description: Summary: Build an automated accuracy validation harness that does NOT rely on a single fixed golden seed set (anchorless). The harness will generate randomized contextual perturbations, replay traffic-like distributions, and run statistical fidelity checks for FP8/INT8 rollouts. Goals: 1) Detect meaningful fidelity regressions from quantized variants with high statistical power while keeping false positives under control. 2) Provide clear pass/fail gates for CI and canary rollouts tied to per-route and aggregated metrics. 3) Integrate with calibration outputs so failing rollouts can be auto-routed to configurable remediation flows (recalibration, fallback to FP16, or abort deploy). Why anchorless: fixed golden sets can be brittle for new prompt distributions and encourage overfitting; by using randomized perturbations + replay cohorts we improve coverage of edge behaviors and surface brittleness across context windows and tokenization boundaries. Key components: - Randomized context perturbation generator: prefix truncation/expansion, paraphrase injection (via small paraphrase model), tokenization-edge injection (split/merge tokens), and noise perturbations (typos, punctuation changes). - Traffic-weighted cohort sampler: sample inputs from production sampling buckets (by token length, route, user-agent) to ensure representative distribution. - Metric suite: token-level accuracy delta, top-k token probability shift, embedding cosine similarity (avg and 5th percentile), ROUGE-L for long-form fidelity, and hallucination signal (extracted factuality checks where available). - Statistical engine: bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation tests for paired comparisons, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across multiple cohorts. - Gating: per-route pass if embedding cosine delta < 0.02 and token-accuracy drop < 0.7% AND aggregate p-value < 0.01; failing cohort can trigger canary-stop. - Calibration workflow integration: ingest calibration traces (per-layer scale factors), run layer-sensitivity checklist (derived from calibration profiles), and attach recommended recalibration candidate to the failure report. - Automation and CI: run on PRs that touch quant codepaths and nightly against rolling production-sampled cohorts. Output: machine-readable report (JSON), human summary (Confluence-friendly), and optional auto-rollout control to Redwood Console via rollout API. Data & privacy: all production inputs used must be hashed and filtered via PII pipeline before inclusion; golden-like synthetic sets stored in S3 with restricted IAM. Success criteria: - Detect introduced regressions of 0.8% token-accuracy drop with >90% power given cohort sizes typical of our routes. - Maintain false-positive rate <5% across a month of nightly runs. - Reduce manual rollback incidents in quant rollouts by 60% over three months. Integration points: Redwood Console (rollout API), CI (GitHub Actions), calibration service (internal service: quant-calib-ctl), observability (Prometheus + Console dashboards).
gating_logic: Per-cohort pass if embedding_cosine_delta < 0.02 AND token_accuracy_delta > -0.7% (i.e. not worse by more than 0.7%) AND aggregate p_value <= 0.01. If any critical customer-impact cohort (customer_impact == high labels) fails, immediate canary stop. Global pass requires all high-impact cohorts to pass and overall FDR-controlled p-values below threshold.
automation_steps: 1) Generate perturbation cohorts from production-sampled bucket
2) Run quantized model inference (FP8/INT8) and FP16 baseline for same inputs
3) Compute metric suite and statistical tests
4) Emit JSON report and upload artifacts to S3
5) Post summary to Confluence and Slack canal #quant-rollouts
6) If gate fails, call Redwood Console rollout API to halt canary and attach recommended remediation
calibration_workflow_notes: Collect calibration traces during inference (activation statistics per layer); run layer-sensitivity delta to find layers with >X% contribution to accuracy loss; attempt automated per-layer recalibration via quant-calib-ctl with candidate scale factors and re-run harness in shadow mode. If automated recalibration improves metrics above pass thresholds, optionally propose auto-rollout patch. All calibration runs must log provenance (model version, seed, calibration profile) and be reversible.
